title: Japanese: Building Sentences
subtitle: Put simple sentences together piece by piece

cards.answer: 私 は 学生 です
cards.note: Watashi wa gakusei desu. は is the topic particle and is then pronounced "wa", not "ha".

cards.answer: これ は 本 です
cards.note: Kore wa hon desu. これ points to something near you, それ to something near the listener, あれ to something farther away.

cards.answer: 私 は 水 を 飲みます
cards.note: Watashi wa mizu o nomimasu. を marks the direct object and is pronounced "o". In Japanese the verb always comes at the end.

cards.answer: パン を 食べます
cards.note: Pan o tabemasu. "I" is usually left out when it is clear from context. パン, by the way, comes from Portuguese.

cards.answer: 駅 に 行きます
cards.note: Eki ni ikimasu. に marks the destination of a movement, as with 行きます (go), 来ます (come) and 帰ります (return home).

cards.answer: これ は お茶 です か
cards.note: Kore wa ocha desu ka. A か at the end of a sentence turns a statement into a question. The word order stays the same.

cards.answer: いい 天気 です ね
cards.note: Ii tenki desu ne. ね at the end of a sentence asks for agreement, much like "right?" or "isn't it?".

cards.answer: 山 は 高い です
cards.note: Yama wa takai desu. い-adjectives like 高い come directly before です. Here です only makes the sentence polite.

cards.answer: 猫 が 好き です
cards.note: Neko ga suki desu. With 好き, the thing you like takes が, not を, because 好き is not a verb but an adjective.

cards.answer: 駅 は どこ です か
cards.note: Eki wa doko desu ka. The question word どこ (where) sits exactly where the answer will go: 駅はあそこです, the station is over there.

cards.answer: 本 を 読みます
cards.note: Hon o yomimasu. 読みます is the polite ます form of 読む (yomu, to read). Japanese has no articles like "a" or "the".

cards.answer: 明日 東京 に 行きます
accept: 明日 は 東京 に 行きます
明日は東京に行きます
cards.note: Ashita Tōkyō ni ikimasu. Relative time words like 明日 or 今日 need no particle, but clock times like 七時 do: 七時に.

cards.prompt: There is a dog over there.
cards.answer: あそこ に 犬 が います
cards.note: Asoko ni inu ga imasu. います is used for living beings, あります for things. Here に marks the place where something is.

cards.answer: 今日 は 静か です
cards.note: Kyō wa shizuka desu. 静か is a な-adjective: the な drops before です but stays before a noun, as in 静かな部屋.

cards.answer: 田中さん は 先生 です
cards.note: Tanaka-san wa sensei desu. You attach さん to other people's names, whether they are men or women, but never to your own.

cards.answer: 映画 を 見ます
cards.note: Eiga o mimasu. 見ます means both to see and to watch. The movie is the object, so it takes を.

cards.answer: コーヒー を 飲みません
accept: コーヒーを飲みません
cards.note: Kōhī o nomimasen. To form the polite negative, replace ます with ません: 飲みます becomes 飲みません.

cards.answer: すし を 食べます か
cards.note: Sushi o tabemasu ka. "You" is left out. Only the か at the end shows that it is a question, and in conversation also a rising voice.

cards.prompt: I get up at seven o'clock.
cards.answer: 七時 に 起きます
cards.note: Shichiji ni okimasu. Clock times take に: 七時に means "at seven o'clock". 時 (ji) is the counter for the hours of the clock.

cards.answer: 花 は きれい です
cards.note: Hana wa kirei desu. きれい ends in い but is a な-adjective. A classic trap: the negative is きれいじゃないです, not きれくない.

cards.prompt: Who is that person over there?
cards.answer: あの 人 は 誰 です か
cards.note: Ano hito wa dare desu ka. あの means "that one over there" and always comes directly before a noun, here 人 (hito, person).

cards.answer: バス を 待ちます
cards.note: Basu o machimasu. In English you wait "for" something; in Japanese the thing you wait for is a direct object with を.

cards.answer: 今日 は 休みます
cards.note: Kyō wa yasumimasu. は makes "today" the topic and often implies a slight contrast: today, unlike other days.

cards.answer: 手紙 を 書きます
cards.note: Tegami o kakimasu. Careful: 手紙 means letter, not toilet paper like the Chinese word written with the same characters.

cards.answer: 時間 が ありません
cards.note: Jikan ga arimasen. ありません is the negative of あります, so literally: "There is no time." The thing that exists, or doesn't, takes が.
